independence_declaration.statement: qa-verifier, session ed63881a-044f-470f-bd1b-844794bf91c7, task T-DG7-REV-QA-R6. At the start I checked the assignment's sha256 (3657e45f326d96e271667b087211212019693377ae2df9d01df351a80a2574b1). In this run I wrote no product implementation, no test in the candidate, no register row, ADR, handover text, repair or delivery decision, and I changed no candidate file. My drivers, probes and mutants ran in a disposable sparse shared clone of 830d7edf under $TMPDIR (removed at the end), on disposable PostgreSQL clusters and kept drill targets. Their scripts are kept as evidence outside the candidate. The implementer roles listed wrote the product, tools, guides, register and the F-DG7-971 repair (ARCH-R6, DO-D9, AN-P7H); the orchestrator decided D-278, froze the candidate and regenerated the handover texts. I formed this verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-6 record, and I have not read them. Their run commits (ded5c9113 code-security, 2ea95b9a6 domain) appeared during my run. I listed only their subjects and paths, and they change no candidate file (the candidate id recomputes unchanged at the end). The round-5 qa-verifier files I read are my own role's earlier, interrupted run.

Each of these gives exit 1 with the exact reason: P1 initiating user; P2 event trigger adoption.check_failed with a schedule-format key; P3b schedule disabled; P4 slot 13:45 outside (13:58:45.715, 14:00:33.441]; P5 key 14:02 names no slot; P6 created 13:59:40.715Z outside; P7 a second, unlisted execution for slot 14:00 ('has 2 executions'); P8 the event re-attributed to a user; P11 the id in the package ('not added'). Observation, not a defect: an operator's run-now inside a slot minute would share the slot's key and be deduplicated by automation_execution_once_key, so it cannot add a second unexplained row. deployment.md and the register notes disclose the rule; known-limitations.md and the release notes do not (F-DG7-972, Low, not blocking).
